primitives.name: Left-Right Bias Map
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using over 22 million shots captured in high-­‐resolution by Noahlytics, we reveal previously hidden systematic biases in entry left-­‐right and entry depth from all positions on the court.
primitives.assumptions: Shot data is uniformly distributed across court positions; deviations follow Gaussian distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At corner 3-point shots, L_R bias exceeds 2 inches, causing >1% shooting percentage loss.

layer2.mapping: Maps spatial shot entry bias to probabilistic shooting accuracy using kernel density estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Mean L_R deviation per court zone, normalized by shot frequency.

primitives.name: Depth Deviation Profile
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using over 22 million shots captured in high-­‐resolution by Noahlytics, we reveal previously hidden systematic biases in entry left-­‐right and entry depth from all positions on the court.
primitives.assumptions: Depth variance correlates with shooting success; data is sampled from consistent shooting mechanics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Shots within 10-inch depth range show >5% variance in shooting percentage.

layer2.mapping: Profiles depth variability against shooting outcomes using regression trees.
layer2.telemetry: Standard deviation of D per shot type, correlated with field goal percentage.

primitives.name: Machine Learning Shooter Ranker
primitives.verbatim_quote: The algorithm outperforms conventional methods and better ranks players by skill-­‐level.
primitives.assumptions: 25-shot sessions provide sufficient statistical power; features are independent and informative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ranking accuracy degrades below 10 shots per session due to insufficient data.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphs spatial shot behavior to latent skill scores via supervised classification.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation accuracy of S-score prediction vs. conventional metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional shooting evaluation relies on summary statistics such as shooting percentage, which are prone to noise from small sample sizes. High-resolution shot capture allows for detailed spatial analysis of shot entry parameters—specifically left-right and depth deviations—which are shown to be systematically biased. These biases are quantified using large-scale data sets (>22M shots) and visualized via heat maps. A machine-learning model trained on 509 players' 25-shot sessions improves upon conventional ranking by capturing nuanced behavioral patterns. The failure mode occurs when sample sizes are too small, leading to unreliable estimates of skill. The dual nature of this approach lies in its ability to both detect systematic errors and correct them through data-driven modeling. The epistemic structure supports causal inference by isolating mechanical components of shooting from random variation.
